ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, the perpendicular bisector of side $AB$ intersects $AB$ at point D and intersects $AC$ at point E. Line $BE$ is drawn. If $AC=5$ and $BC=3$, what is the perimeter of $ \triangle BCE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $DE$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$,\\
it follows that $AE=BE$,\\
Given $AC=5$,\\
it then follows that $BE+CE=AE+CE=AC=5$,\\
Given $BC=3$,\\
the perimeter of $\triangle BCE$ is $BE+CE+BC=5+3=\boxed{8}$.
